questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The most important factor for me was that the language of the destination was English. Furthermore, it was crucial to go to a big city which normally have more cultural diversity than other city and normally also more exchange students.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy to find information provided by University of Copenhagen but I found it a bit more difficult to find information provided by Queen Mary University. However, I think the reason for this is that I'm used to navigating the website and system of University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received assistance in finding my way around campus and assistance at the law reception regarding classes and exams.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Queen Mary University was really good at creating a welcome programme with a lot of activities and opportunities to meet other students. The Law School also arranged their own welcome events for law students which I found really cool.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was not easy and me and my roomies spend a lot of time searching different rental sites and contacting different landlords. We found our flat at
openrent.co.uk
.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed living off campus but only because I ended up with to amazing flatmates. I lived with two other Danish girls from University of Copenhagen but I didn't know them beforehand. I enjoyed living off campus as the area around campus (Mile end) is not at all interesting. It was also really nice that the three of us had a whole flat to host dinners, parties etc. This was not as easy for the exchange students living on campus. However, there were also downside to living off campus. A lot of the others might up every night on campus - just randomly bumping into each other. Furthermore, it was a bit annoying to commute when I attended events, sports and parties on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The official information from Queen Mary was that it was not possible for Erasmus students to get a room on campus. However, a lot of other exchange students applied for a room and got it. I think it was only an option because of Covid-19 but I would really recommend future exchange students to apply for a room on campus even though the official information says it's not possible.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I was a bit confused as to if the registration for exchange students happened on a frist come, first served basis or not. I later found out that it did not.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I was always possible to contact the Law reception where I received an answer really quick.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the four classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: My advice is to contact the host institution to be sure how the process of registration is before the registration opens.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: All of the exchange students at the Law School could only choose between eight classes and we had to choose four in total. It was not the most interesting classes as they were really basic law modules.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Three of the classes I took were at level 6 which is the level for either second or third year of the undergraduate. The last class (contract law) was at level 4 which is the first year of the undergraduate. It was easy to feel the difference between the two levels. Overall, I think the level of courses are more of less the same as UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was more of less the same as UCPH. The structure of each class was also lectures and smaller classes where we solved cases and went through the material from the lecture. Due to Covid all the lectures were online and put on the website after or pre-recorded.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: United Kingdom Human Rights Law, Competition Law, Comparative Constitutional Law and Contract Law I: Formation and Vitiation.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Competition Law as it is interesting and the EU-based. I would also recommend Contract Law as it is really interesting to see how a Common Law jurisdiction deals with contract law.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The local transportation was more expensive than expected. Groceries were less expensive. Restaurants, pubs, bars were the same as expected. Most museums have free entrance making it less expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of different sports club and different societies based on education, religion, belief, country, interests. It was also possible to join academic activities. I was happily surprised with how many activities there were.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus Student Network, a sports club to really connect with the British Students and different societies related to your field of study.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: London has everything. Experience as much of it as possible - restaurants, clubs, pubs, bars, museums, walks around the city, markets, shows, concerts, comedy shows, football matches etc. I also really recommend going on a day trip to Brighton or Oxford.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. I find that the British culture is very similar to the Danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to ALL the welcome events in the beginning, join clubs and societies and go to their events.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any part of the British culture challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How multicultural it is. I liked that you can walk down a fancy street, turn a corner and suddenly it is more young vibrant area.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) try to get a recommendation on campus 
2) explore the city
3) engage in societies, clubs etc on campus

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Queen Mary University of London is a real campus university which is really nice.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange was by far that I had to build a whole new social network which led me to become friends with people around the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: At first it was really difficult to become close friends with people because I'm not used to making jokes and fun side comments etc in English.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: GO to Queen Mary University of London!!! It was the most amazing experience.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
